question: In seasonal variations, the duration of time is not more than:
solution:
The correct answer is **one year. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In seasonal variations, the duration of time typically spans one year. Seasons are cyclical patterns that occur within a yearly cycle. They are influenced by factors such as the tilt of the Earth's axis and its orbit around the Sun.
 
• In most regions, the four primary seasons—spring, summer, autumn (fall), and winter—each last approximately three months. These seasons repeat annually, creating a predictable pattern of changes in temperature, weather conditions, and the growth and behavior of plants and animals.
 
• While there can be variations in the exact timing and intensity of seasons depending on the geographic location, the general timeframe of one year is typically used to define the duration of seasonal variations.
 
• For instance, temperatures over the course of five years can be observed to understand climate patterns, predicting weather conditions, and planning activities accordingly.
